issues.legal_issue: A party to a property sale who has no contractual privity with a lender is not a consumer of the lender’s services under the Consumer Protection Act.
A lender’s liability to pay a property seller is limited to the obligations established by the loan and related agreements, and cannot be inferred to include the entire unpaid sale consideration.
A consumer complaint filed after the statutory limitation period may be entertained only if sufficient cause for delay is shown and the consumer forum records reasons for condoning it.

A borrower who is the link between the seller and the lender, and whose participation is necessary to resolve whether a tripartite agreement exists, must be joined as a necessary party to the consumer complaint.
